title: Split series and represented right torsors for group schemes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and use group schemes and homomorphisms [def-sc-group-scheme], closed and normal subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and connected schemes [def-weil-connected-scheme]. A split series of length $n$ in a $k$-group $H$ consists of smooth connected groups $H=H_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq H_n=1$, each inclusion closed and normal, and homomorphisms $H_i\to Q_i$ presenting the fppf quotient by $H_{i+1}$ in the sense of [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure], with $Q_i$ isomorphic as a group scheme to $\mathbf G_a$ or $\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. The length-zero series means $H$ is the trivial group. Write $H$ split solvable if such a finite series exists. For an arbitrary base scheme $B$ [def-pc-scheme], a $B$-group $H$ and a $B$-scheme $S$, a represented right $H$-torsor is a $B$-scheme $P$, a flat surjective finitely presented morphism $p:P\to S$ [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and a $B$-morphism $a:P\times_B H\to P$ satisfying $a(x,1)=x$ and $a(a(x,g),h)=a(x,gh)$ on every test $B$-scheme, such that the square with top maps $\operatorname{pr}_P,a$ and bottom maps $p,p$ is cartesian. Finite presentation means locally finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. The cartesian square identifies $(x,h)\mapsto(x,a(x,h))$ with an isomorphism $P\times_B H\simeq P\times_S P$. It is Zariski locally trivial if for every point $s\in S$ there is an open immersion $j:U\to S$ [def-pc-scheme] whose image contains $s$ and a morphism $t:U\times_B H\to P$ such that the square with $t,\operatorname{pr}_U,p,j$ is cartesian and $t(u,gh)=a(t(u,g),h)$ on all test $B$-schemes.
